standard_prerequisites.name: Making each curve regular by blowups in closed points
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma resolving an integral curve on a Noetherian surface by blowups in closed points
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces to the case where all the curves are already regular, which is the hypothesis of the separating argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent of the intersection multiplicity when blowing up a common point of two regular curves
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the computation of the behaviour of the intersection multiplicity of two curves meeting at a point under blowing up that point
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the decreasing invariant used in the induction and the separation of curves meeting with multiplicity one.

core_obligations: Reduce to regular curves (proof lines 4398-4401): the resolution lemma for a single curve allows one to assume that each of the given curves is regular.

Decrease the maximal intersection multiplicity (proof lines 4401-4413): for pairs of distinct curves and common points one has the intersection multiplicity; if its maximum over all such pairs and points is larger than one, blowing up in all the points where the maximum is attained strictly decreases that maximum by the computation of the behaviour of the multiplicity under blowing up.

Finish the separation (proof lines 4413-4417): once the maximum equals one, the same lemma shows that blowing up in all the points where it is attained separates the curves, so that the strict transforms are pairwise disjoint regular curves.
proof_roadmap: Make all curves regular by blowups in closed points.
Decrease the maximal intersection multiplicity until it is one.
Separate the remaining intersection points by one more round of blowups.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that finitely many one dimensional integral subschemes of a Noetherian surface each satisfying the resolution conditions can be made into pairwise disjoint regular curves by a finite sequence of blowups in closed points (statement lines 4394-4407). The proof (proof lines 4408-4417) reduces to regular curves, decreases the maximal intersection multiplicity by blowing up in the points where it is attained, and separates the curves when that maximum reaches one. H3: a decreasing invariant argument written out in full.
